answer: A river of agent payments can be protected by requiring each identity to anchor a costly, verifiable signal before it may transact. Like water carving karst, repeated useful work slowly builds a persistent reputation: agents earn trust only by completing priced tasks whose results are independently checked, and their deposit is slashed if they cheat. A Sybil attacker must therefore pay the full price of work, deposits and time for every fake identity, while honest agents reuse one hard-won reputation across the river of commerce, making forgery uneconomic.
